sections.h2: Where is the Mitchell County recording counter?
sections.html:
It is Suite 4 at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle in Bakersville, NC 28705, open on weekdays except holidays. The office records from 8:00 until 4:30. Callers use 828.688.2139, with extension 1402 listed on the county page and extension 1401 given on the office website for fee and recording questions.

Marriage licenses are written until 4:00, cost $60, and are paid by check, cash or money order. Recording itself can be paid in cash, by card, check or money order. The fax number is 828-688-3666.

The staff acts only as a recording office. State law bars the register and employees from practicing law, so any question about what a deed should say goes to an attorney.

sections.h2: What can I search in Mitchell County's online records?
sections.html:
The search site at mitchelldeeds.com holds real estate indexes and images from 1994 to the present. Older material, from 1861 through 1993, sits in an Index Book Viewer under the search menu.

That 1994 line matters for sellers of long-held family land. A deed of trust from the early nineties, a right-of-way, or a division of a family tract may appear only in the older books. The county's services list also covers vital records, an online vital request, document recording standards, index standards and a redaction of personal information page.

  • Search the current index under the seller's name and the prior owner's name.
  • Check the Index Book Viewer when the chain of title reaches back before 1994.
  • Write down every deed of trust you find and confirm each has a recorded satisfaction.

A closing attorney still performs the formal title search. Your own pass simply tells you whether surprises are likely.

sections.h2: What does the Mitchell County Census profile say about local housing?
sections.html:
Mitchell County is small, and the numbers show a settled housing market. Census estimates give 15,062 residents and 8,785 housing units as of July 1, 2025, plus 6,587 households in the multi-year survey ending 2024. Households average 2.21 people.

  • Median gross rent: $813.
  • Monthly owner costs: $1,275 with a mortgage and $389 without.
  • Residents age 65 or older: 27.6 percent.
  • Residents who stayed put over the prior year: 90.1 percent.
  • Building permits counted in 2025: 44.

If you are selling an inherited Mitchell County house, gather the death certificate, the prior deed and any recorded deeds of trust before you talk to a closing attorney.

sections.h2: What are Mitchell County's posted recording charges?
sections.html:
The office's posted fee schedule cites G.S. 161-10 and lists the amounts below, which took effect October 1, 2016.

Mitchell County Register of Deeds posted fees
ItemPosted amount
Deed of trust$64.00 for 35 pages, $4.00 each page after
Other instruments, such as a deed$26.00 for 15 pages, $4.00 each page after
Plat$21.00 a page, 18 by 24 inch sheets only
UCC filing$38.00 for 1 to 2 pages, $45.00 for 3 to 10
SatisfactionNo fee
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each additional

A UCC filing over ten pages is $45.00 plus $2.00 for every page past ten. If a figure matters for your closing, call 828-688-2139 extension 1401 before you send a check.

sections.h2: Does Mitchell County take electronic filings?
sections.html:
Yes, through Simplifile or CSC, the two vendors named on the office's e-recording page.

Law firms and title companies commonly submit this way, so ask your closing attorney which route the firm uses. Anything you file yourself, such as a corrective deed or a gift deed, can go to Suite 4 on a weekday.

sections.h2: Which side pays the deed tax on a Mitchell County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays it at the Bakersville office when the deed is submitted. G.S. 105-228.30 sets the rate at one dollar per $500 of price, rounding a partial $500 up.

The county holds half and sends the state half, minus refunds and a 2 percent county allowance on the state portion.

The Census Bureau's multi-year figures put the middle owner-occupied value at $220,100 and owner occupancy at 76.3 percent, so owners occupy roughly three of every four homes. Your deed price, not any survey average, sets your actual tax.

sections.h2: What vital records and licenses does the Mitchell County office handle?
sections.html:
The office keeps birth, death and marriage records, current and historical, and offers an online vital request. Anyone can get a copy of a vital record, but state law restricts who may receive certified copies, so check the office's vital records page for the list.

A marriage license is $60 and is issued on weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00. Call ahead for the requirements before you drive over.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter in Mitchell County?
sections.html:
G.S. 47-18 says unrecorded transfers and options give way to lien creditors and paying purchasers, and that rank follows the time of registration. Registration happens at the county where the land sits, so Mitchell parcels are registered in Bakersville.

Sellers should ask when the buyer's deed is expected to appear in the index. The register is chosen by county voters every two years under G.S. 161-1.

sections.h2: How do I guard a Mitchell County property against deed fraud?
sections.html:
Sign up for the office's free Fraud Alert system, which alerts you if someone tries to change records tied to your property. It helps most with vacant, rental and inherited houses.

  • Keep copies of every deed, release and satisfaction you receive.
  • Search your name in the index every so often.
  • Record inherited or gifted property promptly.

Buyers on an installment land contract should read Chapter 47H, which requires the seller to put the contract, or a short memorandum of it, on record inside five business days.

sections.h2: Which county offices touch a Mitchell County house sale?
sections.html:
They sit apart but work on the same sale. The register records the deed, the Tax Collector at 61 Crimson Laurel Circle takes payment of the year's bill, and the Tax Assessor at Suite 5, next door to the register, handles relief applications. The collector's calendar has bills going to the January 1 owner of record in August, so the closing papers need to say who covers the year.

A cash buyer of an inherited Mitchell County house can close as-is, with the deed filed through a closing attorney at settlement.

sections.h2: What should veterans and older owners in Mitchell County know?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 946 veterans in Mitchell County for 2020 to 2024, and 27.6 percent of residents are 65 or older. Both groups may qualify for property tax relief, and neither claim is filed with the Register of Deeds.

Applications for exclusions go to the Tax Assessor on Form AV-9. The disabled veteran exclusion also uses Form NCDVA-9, completed first with a Veterans Service Officer. The register's office handles related paper, such as recorded deeds and discharge records, but the relief decision is the assessor's. Ask that office which documents it wants before the next January listing period.

faqs.q: Which phone line reaches Mitchell County recording staff?
faqs.a: Call 828-688-2139 and use extension 1401 for fees and recording, or extension 1402 for the register's line. The office is at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Suite 4, Bakersville.

faqs.q: How old are the Mitchell County records I can search online?
faqs.a: The online index holds real estate indexes and images from 1994 to the present. The 1861 through 1993 material is in the Index Book Viewer on the search menu.

faqs.q: Does filing a mortgage satisfaction cost money in Mitchell County?
faqs.a: No. The office's fee notice lists satisfaction as no fee.

faqs.q: Can my attorney e-record a Mitchell County deed?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile and CSC, the two vendors the office names on its e-recording page.

faqs.q: Will the recording staff tell me what my deed should say?
faqs.a: No. The office says it acts as a recording office only, and state law keeps the register and staff from practicing law. Ask an attorney about wording, title or rights.
